records.label: UCL89

phenotypes.text: absent outer and inner dynein arms on electron microscopy

records.segregation: All affected homozygous; unaffected parents and siblings heterozygous
quotes: Two different mutations were detected: c.323T>C in exon 3 creating missense mutation p.Leu108Pro in family UCL89, and c.406C>T in exon 4 creating nonsense mutation p.Arg136X in family UCL66/67 (Fig. 2b).
Transmission electron microscopy of representative cilia cross sections in family UCL89 showing loss of both outer and inner dynein arms in affected individuals.

For p.Leu108Pro, p.Arg136X and p.Val255CysfsX12, all affected individuals carried homozygous mutations while unaffected parents and siblings carried heterozygous changes consistent with recessive inheritance

records.label: UCL66/67
records.segregation: All affected homozygous; unaffected parents and siblings heterozygous
quotes: Two different mutations were detected: c.323T>C in exon 3 creating missense mutation p.Leu108Pro in family UCL89, and c.406C>T in exon 4 creating nonsense mutation p.Arg136X in family UCL66/67 (Fig. 2b).
The parents of all affected individuals except UCL66/67 III.1 and III.2 are first cousins.

records.label: UCL71
records.segregation: All affected homozygous; unaffected parents and siblings heterozygous
quotes: one family showing evidence of linkage (UCL71, Fig. 2a) had a homozygous single basepair insertion within DNAAF3 exon 6, c.762_763insT, creating a predicted frameshift that generates 11 novel amino acids after a p.Val255Cys change followed by a premature stop codon (p.Val255CysfsX12)
UCL71 is a first-cousin union UK-Pakistani family and this variant was absent from172 control UK-Pakistani chromosomes.

records.label: OP-549
quotes: An additional homozygous single basepair substitution (c.973G>A) identified in a Belgian patient (OP-549) creates a missense variant, p.Ala325Thr.
This residue is not conserved and this variant is likely to be a Caucasian polymorphism.

notes.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) noted that DNAAF3 (C19orf51) on chromosome 19q13 lies within the CILD2 locus mapped in consanguineous Arabic-origin PCD families with absent outer dynein arms, and found homozygous DNAAF3 mutations in 2 of the 3 originally linked families, which showed large regions of marker homozygosity across the locus.
quotes: The DNAAF3 gene resides within a previously described PCD locus (CILD2 locus; MIM 606763) mapped in consanguineous Arabic-origin PCD families characterized by immotile cilia with absent ciliary outer arm dyneins.
We detected homozygous mutations in DNAAF3 in two of the three originally linked families (UCL66/67 and UCL89)

notes.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) reported 10 affected individuals with DNAAF3 mutations who had classic PCD symptoms; 4 of the 10 had situs inversus, and respiratory cilia were immotile with reduced or absent inner and outer dynein arms.
quotes: Clinical features of the 10 patients carrying DNAAF3 mutations are detailed in Supplementary Table 2.
Four out of the 10 affected individuals have situs inversus (Fig. 2).

All the PCD families reported here presented with classic clinical symptoms that included neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent cough and wheezing, nasal discharge and chest infections, sinusitis, otitis media, nasal polyps and bronchiectasis.

notes.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) sequenced DNAAF3 in 112 additional PCD families (107 with outer dynein arm defects) and found only one further family (UCL71) with a homozygous pathogenic mutation; none of the mutations were present in dbSNP, 1000 Genomes, or NHLBI-ESP.
quotes: We sequenced DNAAF3 in 112 additional PCD families, 107 with outer dynein arm defects and 9 with evidence for linkage to the chromosome 19 locus.
None of these mutations are present in the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes or NHLBI-ESP polymorphism databases.

notes.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) found by immunofluorescence that outer arm proteins DNAH5, DNAH9 and DNAI2 and inner arm light chain DNALI1 were absent from respiratory cilia of DNAAF3 patients, with residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 in the apical cytoplasm of some patients, suggesting DNAAF3 is needed for cytoplasmic preassembly of both outer and inner dynein arms.
quotes: ODA components DNAH5 (Fig. 3), DNAH9 and DNAI2 (see Supplementary Fig. 3 and 4), and IDA light chain DNALI1 (Fig. 4) were all absent from the cilia of affected patients.
In some patients, residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 can be seen in the apical cytoplasm, whereas cytoplasmic accumulation of these proteins is not seen in control samples.

notes.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that morpholino knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish caused immotile olfactory placode cilia with reduced or missing dynein arms, body curvature, hydrocephalus, pronephric cysts, otolith defects, and laterality defects, with about half of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos showing reversed or no heart looping.
quotes: Abnormal body axis curvature, with the downward-curving tail (Fig. 5a, b) typical of zebrafish with defects in cilia motility - or assembly was observed in 64% of dnaaf3MOex3 and 78% of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos.
Like PCD patients, the morphant zebrafish embryos displayed perturbed left-right axis patterning, with about half of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos exhibiting either reversed or no heart looping (Fig. 5g).

notes.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) showed that the Chlamydomonas ortholog PF22 is exclusively cytoplasmic; the pf22 null mutant (Trp79X) had paralyzed half-length flagella lacking outer dynein arms and inner dynein arms b and c. Biochemical studies suggested PF22 acts at a later step in dynein preassembly than PF13 and ODA7, such as association of heavy chains with smaller subunits.
quotes: Cell fractionation showed that the MycPF22 protein migrates as a 60 kDa band in cytoplasmic fractions, whereas no equivalent band was seen in axonemal fractions even when loaded at a 50X stoichiometric excess (Fig. 1d).

therefore if PF22 acts as a co-chaperone, it likely works at a later step than PF13 and ODA7 such as the stabilization of heavy chains or the joining of heavy chains and smaller subunits into a larger complex, rather than folding of globular head domains.

notes.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) noted that human DNAAF3 encodes a 588-amino acid protein whose transcript increased 5.62-fold during cilia formation, and that single homologs exist in organisms with motile cilia but not those lacking them.
quotes: The human DAB1 orthologous gene DNAAF3 on human chromosome 19q13 (previously designated C19orf51) encodes a 588 amino acid protein (Genbank NP_849159). It was identified in expression studies as a potential cilia-related gene whose transcript abundance increased 5.62-fold during cilia formation.

notes.statement: Meeks et al. (2000) performed a genome scan in 5 Arabic families with primary ciliary dyskinesia. Using GENEHUNTER, they obtained a maximum multipoint lod score (HLOD) of 4.4 on chromosome 19q13.3-qter at alpha (proportion of linked families) = 0.7, and recombinations at D19S572 and D19S218 defined a 15-cM critical region.
quotes: Using GENEHUNTER, a maximal multipoint lod score (HLOD) of 4.4 was obtained on chromosome 19q13.3-qter at alpha (proportion of linked families) = 0.7.
A 15 cM critical region is defined by recombinations at D19S572 and D19S218.

notes.statement: Meeks et al. (2000) concluded that their data provided significant evidence for a PCD locus on chromosome 19q and confirmed locus heterogeneity.
quotes: These data provide significant evidence for a PCD locus on chromosome 19q and confirm locus heterogeneity.

notes.statement: Meeks et al. (2000) described primary ciliary dyskinesia as an autosomal recessive condition with chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility, with situs inversus in 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome). They noted that the phenotype results from defective ciliary function associated with ultrastructural abnormalities including absent dynein arms, absent radial spokes, and disturbed ciliary orientation.
quotes: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive condition characterised by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility. Situs inversus occurs in 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome).

The clinical phenotype is caused by defective ciliary function associated with a range of ultrastructural abnormalities including absent dynein arms, absent radial spokes, and disturbed ciliary orientation.

notes.statement: Meeks et al. (2000) stated that primary ciliary dyskinesia has an estimated incidence of 1 in 20,000 live births.
quotes: It has an estimated incidence of 1 in 20 000 live births.
